name: Threshold Dimension of Addressing
details: Scope: complete-code subfamily n=2^r, r>=1; at n=1 the value is zero. No exact formula is asserted for arbitrary incomplete injective encodings. The earlier r+1 formula incorrectly reused the same all-one-address concept twice.
proof: Write n=2^r. Projection to all r bit coordinates is the full cube, giving threshold dimension at least r. Every concept has at most r+1 positive coordinates, so a longer witness could only have size r+1. Its full trace must come from the unique concept positive at its retained primary coordinate, and hence uses that primary coordinate and all r bit coordinates. The preceding trace in a chain deletes one coordinate. If it deletes a bit, it still contains the primary coordinate and would require the same concept with a changed bit. If it deletes the primary coordinate, it has all r bits positive, again forcing the same all-one-address concept. Both are impossible. Thus the dimension is r. At n=1 the single concept has no varying coordinate and the dimension is zero.
